def merge_intervals(intervals: list) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    # Filter out empty intervals and convert to tuples
    valid_intervals = [(start, end) for start, end in intervals if end > start]
    
    # Sort by start position
    valid_intervals.sort()
    
    if not valid_intervals:
        return []
    
    # Merge overlapping/touching intervals
    merged = []
    current_start, current_end = valid_intervals[0]
    
    for start, end in valid_intervals[1:]:
        # If current interval overlaps or touches the next one, merge them
        if start <= current_end:
            current_end = max(current_end, end)
        else:
            # No overlap, save current and start a new one
            merged.append((current_start, current_end))
            current_start, current_end = start, end
    
    # Don't forget to add the last interval
    merged.append((current_start, current_end))
    
    return merged
